scene.note: The browser only follows HTML, so Dilys's words become a page once index.html says what each part of it is.

steps.note: Dilys typed her words into index.html, with no HTML at all.
The browser opens the file and looks at the top of the file to learn what kind of page it is.
Put the doctype above everything else, and wrap the rest in one root element that says the page is in English.
Now the browser treats the file as a modern page and knows its language.
Today the tab only shows the file name, which tells a visitor nothing.
Add a head inside the root element. It holds facts about the page that are not shown on it.
The character set tells the browser how the letters are stored, so none come out as odd symbols.
The title travels to the tab, and the tab shows the studio's name.
On the page, the studio name and both sentences run together in one line.
Add a body after the head and move her words into it.
The studio name becomes the one main heading, and each sentence gets a paragraph of its own.
The browser shows the heading big and puts space between the paragraphs.
